1	# Nope-Mode
     2	
     3	Selected apps go silent and un-openable — on a schedule, or on demand.
     4	
     5	A cleanroom equivalent of Google's Focus Mode, for GrapheneOS, where Digital
     6	Wellbeing does not exist. No accounts, no network, no analytics.
     7	
     8	**Status:** specification only. See [design.md](design.md) for the full spec
     9	and [todo.md](todo.md) for the build plan.
    10	
    11	## What it does
    12	
    13	- Pick the apps that are allowed to bother you, and the ones that aren't.
    14	- When Nope-Mode is on, blocked apps produce **no notifications, no sound, no
    15	  vibration**, and **cannot be opened**.
    16	- Turn it on by hand, from a quick-settings tile, or let the schedule do it.
    17	- **Default schedule: 20:00 → 08:00, daily.**
    18	
    19	## How it works
    20	
    21	Nope-Mode runs as a **device owner** and uses the platform's
    22	`setPackagesSuspended` — the same mechanism behind Google's Focus Mode. A
    23	suspended app cannot show notifications, play audio, raise dialogs, or launch.
    24	It survives reboots, which a Shizuku-based approach does not.
    25	
    26	Where device owner isn't provisioned, Nope-Mode falls back to a
    27	notification listener plus an accessibility service. That tier works
    28	everywhere but is leakier — a notification may make a sound before it is
    29	suppressed.
    30	
    31	## Setup
    32	
    33	Device owner can **only** be provisioned on a device with **no accounts added**.
    34	Install the APK on a freshly reset device, then:
    35	
    36	```sh
    37	adb shell dpm set-device-owner com.piercingxx.nopemode/.admin.NopeDeviceAdminReceiver
    38	```
    39	
    40	Adding a Google account first closes this window, and reopening it requires a
    41	factory reset.
    42	
    43	Device owner is a full MDM role and carries real tradeoffs — some banking and
    44	DRM apps refuse to run on managed devices. Nope-Mode always exposes a
    45	**Relinquish device owner** action so this is reversible without a wipe. Read
    46	§2.2 of [design.md](design.md) before provisioning.
    47	
    48	## Requirements
    49	
    50	- Android 7.0+ (minSdk 24), built and tested against GrapheneOS on a Pixel 9 Pro
    51	- Device owner for full enforcement; otherwise the fallback tier
    52	
    53	## License
    54	
    55	Copyright (c) 2026 PiercingXX. All rights reserved.
    56	
    57	No code is derived from Hail, NotiFilter, DetoxDroid, or any other GPL project.
    58	Nope-Mode is a cleanroom implementation written against public Android API
    59	documentation.

1	# Nope-Mode — Design Specification
     2	
     3	Android app for GrapheneOS. Selected apps go silent and un-openable, on a
     4	schedule or on demand.
     5	
     6	A cleanroom equivalent of Google's Focus Mode, which does not exist on
     7	GrapheneOS because Digital Wellbeing is not shipped and cannot be installed
     8	from Play.
     9	
    10	**Status:** WS1 and WS4 landed. WS2, WS3, WS5–WS10 unbuilt.
    11	**Target:** Pixel 9 Pro (`caiman`), GrapheneOS, Android 17 / SDK 37.
    12	**Provisioned:** device owner is live on the target device as of 2026-08-03.
    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## 1. Cleanroom provenance
    17	
    18	This repository is **all rights reserved**. Every close prior art is
    19	**GPL-3.0**. Copying from them would force this project to GPL.
    20	
    21	**What was studied:** F-Droid listings, README files, published feature
    22	descriptions, user-facing behavior, and official Android API documentation.
    23	
    24	**What was never opened:** the source code of Hail, NotiFilter, DetoxDroid,
    25	Curbox Detox, or Open TimeLimit.
    26	
    27	Behavioral *ideas* are not copyrightable; expression is. What follows is
    28	derived from documented behavior and the public Android SDK. Anyone extending
    29	this project must hold the same line: **read their docs, never their source.**
    30	
    31	### Prior art and what each contributed
    32	
    33	| Project | License | What was taken (behavior only) |
    34	|---|---|---|
    35	| Google Focus Mode | proprietary | The target behavior itself: pick distracting apps, pause them, schedule it, and offer a **bounded** "take a break" (5/15/30 min). Grayed-out icons as the paused signal. |
    36	| [Hail](https://github.com/aistra0528/Hail) | GPL-3.0 | Confirmation that suspend-based freezing is the right mechanism, and that disable/hide/suspend are meaningfully different. |
    37	| [NotiFilter](https://github.com/BURG3R5/NotiFilter) | GPL-3.0 | That notification-listener filtering is viable as a fallback, and that scheduling windows belong on the filter itself. |
    38	| [DetoxDroid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.flx_apps.digitaldetox/) | GPL-3.0 | **"Protection always on"** — you pause deliberately, it auto-resumes, and there is a *minimum interval between pauses*. This is the single most important behavioral idea in the whole design (§11). |
    39	| [Curbox Detox](https://f-droid.org/packages/neth.iecal.curbox/) | FOSS | Graduated bypass resistance: strict / timed / per-attempt / challenge / capped attempt counts. |
    40	
    41	---
    42	
    43	## 2. Requirements
    44	
    45	**R1.** Maintain a user-selected list of blocked apps.
    46	**R2.** When active, blocked apps emit no notification, no sound, no vibration.
    47	**R3.** When active, blocked apps cannot be opened.
    48	**R4.** Activate manually, from a quick-settings tile, or on a schedule.
    49	**R5.** Ship with a default schedule of **20:00 → 08:00, every day**, enabled.
    50	**R6.** Deactivating restores every app to exactly its prior state.
    51	**R7.** Survive reboots, including a reboot in the middle of a window.
    52	**R8.** Never silently under-enforce. If a block fails, say so.
    53	
    54	### Non-goals
    55	
    56	- Usage analytics, screen-time charts, streaks, leaderboards.
    57	- Per-app time budgets. Nope-Mode is binary: blocked or not.
    58	- Website or URL blocking, keyword filtering of notification content.
    59	- Grayscale, doomscroll detection, Extra Dim. (DetoxDroid does these; they are
    60	  a different product.)
    61	- Parental controls, remote administration, accounts, telemetry.
    62	- **Any network access whatsoever.** The app declares no `INTERNET` permission
    63	  and must never gain one.
    64	
    65	---
    66	
    67	## 3. Decisions
    68	
    69	| # | Decision | Rationale |
    70	|---|---|---|
    71	| D1 | **Device owner is the primary enforcement mechanism** | `setPackagesSuspended` is the only no-root API delivering R2 *and* R3, and it survives reboots (R7). Shizuku was rejected: it must be re-armed after every reboot, silently breaking an unattended overnight schedule — precisely the failure the app exists to prevent. |
    72	| D2 | **Notification listener + accessibility is the fallback tier** | Zero provisioning, works anywhere. Strictly weaker (§8.2) but the app is never useless. |
    73	| D3 | **Blocked apps are un-openable, not merely silent** | Full Focus Mode parity. Suspension delivers R2 and R3 in one call, so this costs nothing extra. |
    74	| D4 | **Kotlin + Views, no Compose** | Matches PiercingXX-Launcher exactly. |
    75	| D5 | **Public repo, all rights reserved** | Matches the launcher. Consequence: cleanroom discipline per §1, permanently. |
    76	| D6 | **Room + Gson** | Same stack as the launcher, so backup JSON conventions carry over. |
    77	| D7 | **Breaks are always time-bounded** | An unbounded "off" turns a schedule into a suggestion. See §11. |
    78	| D8 | **State is derived, never accumulated** | A pure function of (now, schedules, override). Makes missed or duplicated alarms harmless. See §9. |
    79	
    80	### 3.1 Device owner — the standing cost
    81	
    82	Device owner is a full MDM role, and this is a real tradeoff, not a formality:
    83	
    84	- Settings will report the device as managed.
    85	- **Some apps refuse to run on managed devices** — banking, certain DRM video.
    86	- The user cannot remove it through Settings. Nope-Mode **must** expose
    87	  *Relinquish device owner* → `clearDeviceOwnerApp()`. Without it the only exit
    88	  is a factory reset. Implemented in WS4; do not remove it.
    89	- Only one device owner may exist. Nope-Mode holds that slot for the life of
    90	  the install.
    91	
    92	### 3.2 Provisioning window (historical, now satisfied)
    93	
    94	Device owner can only be set on a device with **zero accounts**:
    95	
    96	```sh
    97	adb shell dpm set-device-owner \
    98	    com.piercingxx.nopemode/.admin.NopeDeviceAdminReceiver
    99	```
   100	
   101	This was provisioned on 2026-08-03 after a factory reset. **It cost one wipe to
   102	learn that opening the Google apps first closes the window.** If device owner is
   103	ever relinquished, regaining it costs another full reset — treat it as
   104	non-renewable.
   105	
   106	---
   107	
   108	## 4. Platform mechanics
   109	
   110	Authoritative behavior of `DevicePolicyManager.setPackagesSuspended`, from
   111	Android documentation. The whole design rests on this, so it is quoted rather
   112	than paraphrased loosely.
   113	
   114	A suspended package:
   115	
   116	- cannot start activities;
   117	- has its **notifications hidden**;
   118	- does **not** appear in the recents / overview screen;
   119	- cannot show toasts, dialogs, or snackbars;
   120	- **cannot play audio or vibrate the device**;
   121	- shows a system "app is paused" dialog when tapped;
   122	- is **grayed out in the launcher**.
   123	
   124	That single call satisfies R2 and R3 completely. No notification listener, no
   125	accessibility service, no DND manipulation is required at this tier.
   126	
   127	### 4.1 Packages that cannot be suspended
   128	
   129	The platform refuses these outright. The picker must exclude them at
   130	**selection time**, not fail at enforcement time:
   131	
   132	- Device admins — **this includes Nope-Mode itself**
   133	- The **active launcher** (suspending it bricks the home screen)
   134	- The required **package installer**, **uninstaller**, and **verifier**
   135	- The **default dialer**
   136	- The **permission controller**
   137	
   138	Two more that the platform *permits* but which must be guarded anyway:
   139	
   140	- **The active input method.** Suspending the keyboard leaves the user unable
   141	  to type — including unable to type their way out. Hard-block it.
   142	- **The default SMS handler.** Permitted, and a legitimate choice for some, but
   143	  it silences 2FA codes. Require an explicit confirmation; never reachable via
   144	  bulk-select.
   145	
   146	`setPackagesSuspended` **returns the array of packages it could not suspend.**
   147	Never discard it (R8).
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## 5. Architecture
   152	
   153	```
   154	        ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
   155	        │           NopeController           │  owns desired state
   156	        │  derive(now, schedules, override)  │  talks to no Android API
   157	        └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘
   158	                           │ desired: Set<packageName>
   159	        ┌──────────────────▼─────────────────┐
   160	        │         Enforcer (interface)       │
   161	        └────────┬──────────────────┬────────┘
   162	                 │                  │
   163	      ┌──────────▼──────┐   ┌───────▼─────────────────┐
   164	      │ SuspendEnforcer │   │    FallbackEnforcer     │
   165	      │  device owner   │   │  listener + a11y        │
   166	      └─────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘
   167	```
   168	
   169	`NopeController` computes *what should be true* and hands it to an `Enforcer`.
   170	It imports nothing from `android.*`. That is what makes the scheduling logic —
   171	the part that must be correct — testable on the JVM with no device.
   172	
   173	Tier selection, re-evaluated whenever admin state changes:
   174	
   175	```
   176	if (dpm.isDeviceOwnerApp(packageName)) SuspendEnforcer else FallbackEnforcer
   177	```
   178	
   179	The active tier must be **visible in the UI at all times**. A user on the
   180	fallback tier is getting weaker protection and has to know it (R8).
   181	
   182	---
   183	
   184	## 6. State model
   185	
   186	The heart of the app. Everything else is plumbing.
   187	
   188	```kotlin
   189	sealed interface Override {
   190	    data object None : Override
   191	    data class ForceOn(val until: Instant?) : Override   // null = indefinite
   192	    data class Break(val until: Instant) : Override      // ALWAYS bounded
   193	}
   194	
   195	fun isActive(now, schedules, override): Boolean = when (override) {
   196	    is Override.ForceOn -> override.until == null || now < override.until
   197	    is Override.Break   -> if (now < override.until) false
   198	                           else scheduleSaysActive(now, schedules)
   199	    Override.None       -> scheduleSaysActive(now, schedules)
   200	}
   201	```
   202	
   203	| Override | Schedule | Result |
   204	|---|---|---|
   205	| `None` | inactive | inactive |
   206	| `None` | active | **active** |
   207	| `ForceOn(null)` | either | **active**, indefinitely |
   208	| `ForceOn(t)`, now < t | either | **active** |
   209	| `ForceOn(t)`, now ≥ t | — | expires → re-derive from schedule |
   210	| `Break(t)`, now < t | active | inactive (break running) |
   211	| `Break(t)`, now ≥ t | active | **active** — break expired, auto-resume |
   212	
   213	**`Break` has no unbounded variant, by construction.** There is no way to
   214	express "off until I say so". This is D7, and it is the difference between a
   215	schedule and a suggestion.
   216	
   217	---
   218	
   219	## 7. Scheduling
   220	
   221	```kotlin
   222	data class Schedule(
   223	    val id: Long,
   224	    val startMinuteOfDay: Int,   // 20:00 -> 1200
   225	    val endMinuteOfDay: Int,     // 08:00 -> 480
   226	    val daysMask: Int,           // bit 0 = Monday .. bit 6 = Sunday
   227	    val enabled: Boolean,
   228	)
   229	```
   230	
   231	**Windows cross midnight.** `end <= start` means the window wraps into the next
   232	day. The shipped default (1200 → 480) does exactly this, so **the wrap is the
   233	common path, not an edge case.** Test it first, before the non-wrapping case.
   234	
   235	`daysMask` refers to the day the window **starts**. A Friday-enabled 20:00→08:00
   236	window runs Friday 20:00 through Saturday 08:00. A user unchecking Saturday
   237	expects Saturday *night* to be unblocked, not Saturday *morning* — say so in the
   238	UI, because both readings are defensible.
   239	
   240	### 7.1 Reconciliation, not event-chasing
   241	
   242	```kotlin
   243	fun shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean
   244	```
   245	
   246	Pure. State is **always** obtained by calling this, never by accumulating alarm
   247	events (D8). Alarms merely prompt re-evaluation. A missed, late, or duplicated
   248	alarm therefore cannot corrupt state — the system is self-healing.
   249	
   250	`reconcile()` runs on: boot completed, alarm fired, app foregrounded, tile
   251	clicked, schedule edited, blocked-list edited, break started or expired,
   252	`TIME_SET`, `TIMEZONE_CHANGED`.
   253	
   254	### 7.2 Alarms
   255	
   256	- `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP, …)` for **the next boundary only**;
   257	  recompute and re-arm after each fire. Never pre-schedule a chain.
   258	- `USE_EXACT_ALARM` (API 33+), plus `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` for the minSdk 24
   259	  range. If `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is false, degrade to
   260	  `setAndAllowWhileIdle` **and show a persistent warning** — an inexact 20:00
   261	  boundary can drift by minutes, which is visible and wrong.
   262	- `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` → re-arm and reconcile. Without this the schedule
   263	  dies at the first reboot, which is exactly the Shizuku failure D1 rejected.
   264	
   265	---
   266	
   267	## 8. Enforcement tiers
   268	
   269	### 8.1 SuspendEnforcer — primary
   270	
   271	```kotlin
   272	dpm.setPackagesSuspended(admin, packages, true)   // engage
   273	dpm.setPackagesSuspended(admin, packages, false)  // release
   274	```
   275	
   276	Order of operations matters for crash safety:
   277	
   278	1. Write intended packages to `suspend_record`.
   279	2. Call `setPackagesSuspended(…, true)`.
   280	3. Inspect the returned failure array; record and surface any failures.
   281	
   282	Releasing reverses it: suspend-false first, then clear `suspend_record` only
   283	for packages that actually released.
   284	
   285	If the process dies between (1) and (2), reconcile-on-boot sees a record with
   286	nothing suspended and re-derives — harmless. If it dies between (2) and (3),
   287	the record is authoritative and the apps get released correctly. **Writing the
   288	record first is what makes a crash recoverable rather than stranding apps.**
   289	
   290	### 8.2 FallbackEnforcer — no device owner
   291	
   292	**a) `NopeNotificationListener : NotificationListenerService`**
   293	On `onNotificationPosted`, if the package is blocked and the mode is active,
   294	`cancelNotification(sbn.key)`; prefer `snoozeNotification(key, duration)` where
   295	it fits, since it suppresses re-post without a visible dismissal.
   296	
   297	> **Stated limitation, which must appear in the UI verbatim in spirit:** the
   298	> notification has already been posted when the listener sees it, so **the alert
   299	> sound may play before suppression**. This tier delivers "the notification goes
   300	> away", not "the notification never made a sound". It does not satisfy R2.
   301	
   302	**b) `NopeAccessibilityService : AccessibilityService`**
   303	On `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED`, read the foreground package; if blocked and
   304	active, launch `BlockedActivity` with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`. Debounce to
   305	avoid launch loops.
   306	
   307	Do **not** use `performGlobalAction(GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK)` as the block — it
   308	fights the user's navigation and behaves inconsistently across launchers.
   309	
   310	---
   311	
   312	## 9. Breaks and anti-bypass
   313	
   314	Adopted from DetoxDroid's "protection always on" and Curbox's graduated
   315	resistance. Without this, a schedule is decoration — at 2am the user simply
   316	turns it off.
   317	
   318	**Baseline (ship in WS7):**
   319	
   320	- **Take a break** offers **5 / 15 / 30 minutes**, matching Focus Mode. No
   321	  custom-duration field, no "until I turn it back on".
   322	- Breaks **auto-resume**. There is no user action required to re-engage.
   323	- A break shows a persistent countdown notification from Nope-Mode itself, so
   324	  it is never ambiguous whether protection is on.
   325	
   326	**Friction (WS7, configurable, default on):**
   327	
   328	- **Minimum interval between breaks** — default 30 minutes. Prevents chaining
   329	  5-minute breaks into an unbounded evening.
   330	- **Break budget** — default 3 per active window. Exhausted means exhausted.
   331	
   332	**Deferred, explicitly out of scope for v1:**
   333	
   334	- Typing a sentence, scanning a QR code, or a commitment password. These are
   335	  proven patterns (Curbox, DetoxDroid) but they are anti-features until the
   336	  basics are solid. Revisit only if the baseline proves too easy to defeat.
   337	
   338	Every friction setting must be **editable only while Nope-Mode is inactive.**
   339	Otherwise the 2am workaround is simply to raise the break budget.
   340	
   341	---
   342	
   343	## 10. Data model (Room)
   344	
   345	```
   346	blocked_app      packageName TEXT PK, addedAt INTEGER
   347	schedule         id INTEGER PK, startMinuteOfDay INT, endMinuteOfDay INT,
   348	                 daysMask INT, enabled INT
   349	app_state        id INTEGER PK (=1), overrideKind TEXT, overrideUntil INTEGER NULL,
   350	                 lastReconcileAt INTEGER
   351	suspend_record   packageName TEXT PK, suspendedAt INTEGER
   352	break_log        id INTEGER PK, startedAt INTEGER, durationMinutes INT
   353	```
   354	
   355	- `suspend_record` — crash safety net (§8.1). On boot, anything present here
   356	  but no longer scheduled to be blocked is released. Without this table a crash
   357	  mid-activation can leave apps permanently suspended with no UI to recover them.
   358	- `break_log` — enforces minimum interval and break budget (§9).
   359	
   360	Seed migration inserts the default schedule `(1200, 480, all days, enabled)`.
   361	
   362	---
   363	
   364	## 11. UI
   365	
   366	Five screens. Views + viewBinding, AMOLED-black monochrome, matching the
   367	launcher.
   368	
   369	1. **Home** — large active/inactive state; the *reason* ("scheduled until
   370	   08:00", "break, 12 min left"); master toggle; **Take a break** button when
   371	   active; blocked-app count; **enforcement-tier badge**.
   372	2. **Blocked apps** — searchable list of launchable packages with icons and
   373	   checkboxes. Packages from §4.1 shown disabled **with the reason inline** —
   374	   not silently absent, or the user assumes it's blocked when it isn't.
   375	3. **Schedules** — list, add, edit, delete. Time pickers plus day-of-week
   376	   selector. Default row pre-seeded. Show the wrap explicitly: *"20:00 tonight
   377	   → 08:00 tomorrow"*.
   378	4. **Settings** — break duration options, minimum interval, break budget.
   379	   **Locked while active** (§9).
   380	5. **Setup / status** — tier, provisioning command, fallback permission grants,
   381	   and **Relinquish device owner** with a plain-language warning.
   382	
   383	`BlockedActivity` — the fallback tier's full-screen interstitial. One word,
   384	*Nope.*, the app name, and when the block lifts.
   385	
   386	### 11.1 Quick Settings tile
   387	
   388	`NopeTileService : TileService` — toggles `ForceOn` / clears it. Label and state
   389	must track derived state even when changed elsewhere
   390	(`requestListeningState`).
   391	
   392	On the target device this tile replaces the dead Digital Wellbeing Focus Mode
   393	tile, which cannot work on GrapheneOS. Note the shade layout **cannot be set
   394	programmatically on Android 17** — `sysui_qs_tiles` is vestigial and the real
   395	storage is root-only — so tile placement is always a manual user step. Do not
   396	waste effort automating it.
   397	
   398	---
   399	
   400	## 12. Manifest
   401	
   402	```xml
   403	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED"/>
   404	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM"/>
   405	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM"/>
   406	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES"/>
   407	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"/>
   408	<!-- deliberately NO android.permission.INTERNET -->
   409	```
   410	
   411	Components: `NopeDeviceAdminReceiver` (+ `res/xml/device_admin.xml`),
   412	`NopeNotificationListener`, `NopeAccessibilityService`, `NopeTileService`,
   413	`BootReceiver` (`BOOT_COMPLETED`, `TIME_SET`, `TIMEZONE_CHANGED`).
   414	
   415	`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is for Nope-Mode's own break countdown only.
   416	
   417	The absent `INTERNET` permission is a verifiable privacy claim. Keep it true;
   418	it is checkable with `aapt2 dump permissions`.
   419	
   420	---
   421	
   422	## 13. Package layout
   423	
   424	```
   425	com.piercingxx.nopemode
   426	├── admin/      NopeDeviceAdminReceiver, DeviceOwnerManager          [WS4 done]
   427	├── core/       NopeController, ScheduleEvaluator, Override, BreakPolicy
   428	├── enforce/    Enforcer, SuspendEnforcer, FallbackEnforcer
   429	├── data/       entities, DAOs, NopeDatabase, BackupJson
   430	├── schedule/   AlarmScheduler, BootReceiver
   431	├── service/    NopeNotificationListener, NopeAccessibilityService,
   432	│               NopeTileService
   433	└── ui/         HomeActivity, BlockedAppsActivity, SchedulesActivity,
   434	                SettingsActivity, SetupActivity, BlockedActivity
   435	```
   436	
   437	---
   438	
   439	## 14. Failure modes
   440	
   441	| Scenario | Required behaviour |
   442	|---|---|
   443	| Crash while apps suspended | `suspend_record` + boot reconcile releases them |
   444	| Reboot mid-window | `BootReceiver` reconciles; apps re-suspend |
   445	| Exact alarm permission denied | Degrade to inexact, warn persistently, keep reconciling |

    13	 * they have already posted, so a sound may escape first. Callers must be able
    14	 * to tell the user which one they are actually on — silently degrading would
    15	 * make the app claim protection it isn't providing.
    16	 */

    18	
    19	    private val appContext = context.applicationContext
    20	    private val dpm =
    21	        appContext.getSystemService(Context.DEVICE_POLICY_SERVICE) as DevicePolicyManager
    22	
    23	    enum class Tier { DEVICE_OWNER, FALLBACK }
    24	
    25	    val adminComponent: ComponentName
    26	        get() = NopeDeviceAdminReceiver.componentName(appContext)
    27	
    28	    fun isDeviceOwner(): Boolean =
    29	        dpm.isDeviceOwnerApp(appContext.packageName)
    30	
    31	    fun tier(): Tier =
    32	        if (isDeviceOwner()) Tier.DEVICE_OWNER else Tier.FALLBACK

1	# Nope-Mode — Design Specification
     2	
     3	Android app for GrapheneOS. Selected apps go silent and un-openable, on a
     4	schedule or on demand.
     5	
     6	A cleanroom equivalent of Google's Focus Mode, which does not exist on
     7	GrapheneOS because Digital Wellbeing is not shipped and cannot be installed
     8	from Play.
     9	
    10	**Status:** WS1 and WS4 landed. WS2, WS3, WS5–WS10 unbuilt.
    11	**Target:** Pixel 9 Pro (`caiman`), GrapheneOS, Android 17 / SDK 37.
    12	**Provisioned:** device owner is live on the target device as of 2026-08-03.
    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## 1. Cleanroom provenance
    17	
    18	This repository is **all rights reserved**. Every close prior art is
    19	**GPL-3.0**. Copying from them would force this project to GPL.
    20	
    21	**What was studied:** F-Droid listings, README files, published feature
    22	descriptions, user-facing behavior, and official Android API documentation.
    23	
    24	**What was never opened:** the source code of Hail, NotiFilter, DetoxDroid,
    25	Curbox Detox, or Open TimeLimit.
    26	
    27	Behavioral *ideas* are not copyrightable; expression is. What follows is
    28	derived from documented behavior and the public Android SDK. Anyone extending
    29	this project must hold the same line: **read their docs, never their source.**
    30	
    31	### Prior art and what each contributed
    32	
    33	| Project | License | What was taken (behavior only) |
    34	|---|---|---|
    35	| Google Focus Mode | proprietary | The target behavior itself: pick distracting apps, pause them, schedule it, and offer a **bounded** "take a break" (5/15/30 min). Grayed-out icons as the paused signal. |
    36	| [Hail](https://github.com/aistra0528/Hail) | GPL-3.0 | Confirmation that suspend-based freezing is the right mechanism, and that disable/hide/suspend are meaningfully different. |
    37	| [NotiFilter](https://github.com/BURG3R5/NotiFilter) | GPL-3.0 | That notification-listener filtering is viable as a fallback, and that scheduling windows belong on the filter itself. |
    38	| [DetoxDroid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.flx_apps.digitaldetox/) | GPL-3.0 | **"Protection always on"** — you pause deliberately, it auto-resumes, and there is a *minimum interval between pauses*. This is the single most important behavioral idea in the whole design (§11). |
    39	| [Curbox Detox](https://f-droid.org/packages/neth.iecal.curbox/) | FOSS | Graduated bypass resistance: strict / timed / per-attempt / challenge / capped attempt counts. |
    40	
    41	---
    42	
    43	## 2. Requirements
    44	
    45	**R1.** Maintain a user-selected list of blocked apps.
    46	**R2.** When active, blocked apps emit no notification, no sound, no vibration.
    47	**R3.** When active, blocked apps cannot be opened.
    48	**R4.** Activate manually, from a quick-settings tile, or on a schedule.
    49	**R5.** Ship with a default schedule of **20:00 → 08:00, every day**, enabled.
    50	**R6.** Deactivating restores every app to exactly its prior state.
    51	**R7.** Survive reboots, including a reboot in the middle of a window.
    52	**R8.** Never silently under-enforce. If a block fails, say so.
    53	
    54	### Non-goals
    55	
    56	- Usage analytics, screen-time charts, streaks, leaderboards.
    57	- Per-app time budgets. Nope-Mode is binary: blocked or not.
    58	- Website or URL blocking, keyword filtering of notification content.
    59	- Grayscale, doomscroll detection, Extra Dim. (DetoxDroid does these; they are
    60	  a different product.)
    61	- Parental controls, remote administration, accounts, telemetry.
    62	- **Any network access whatsoever.** The app declares no `INTERNET` permission
    63	  and must never gain one.
    64	
    65	---
    66	
    67	## 3. Decisions
    68	
    69	| # | Decision | Rationale |
    70	|---|---|---|
    71	| D1 | **Device owner is the primary enforcement mechanism** | `setPackagesSuspended` is the only no-root API delivering R2 *and* R3, and it survives reboots (R7). Shizuku was rejected: it must be re-armed after every reboot, silently breaking an unattended overnight schedule — precisely the failure the app exists to prevent. |
    72	| D2 | **Notification listener + accessibility is the fallback tier** | Zero provisioning, works anywhere. Strictly weaker (§8.2) but the app is never useless. |
    73	| D3 | **Blocked apps are un-openable, not merely silent** | Full Focus Mode parity. Suspension delivers R2 and R3 in one call, so this costs nothing extra. |
    74	| D4 | **Kotlin + Views, no Compose** | Matches PiercingXX-Launcher exactly. |
    75	| D5 | **Public repo, all rights reserved** | Matches the launcher. Consequence: cleanroom discipline per §1, permanently. |
    76	| D6 | **Room + Gson** | Same stack as the launcher, so backup JSON conventions carry over. |
    77	| D7 | **Breaks are always time-bounded** | An unbounded "off" turns a schedule into a suggestion. See §11. |
    78	| D8 | **State is derived, never accumulated** | A pure function of (now, schedules, override). Makes missed or duplicated alarms harmless. See §9. |
    79	
    80	### 3.1 Device owner — the standing cost
    81	
    82	Device owner is a full MDM role, and this is a real tradeoff, not a formality:
    83	
    84	- Settings will report the device as managed.
    85	- **Some apps refuse to run on managed devices** — banking, certain DRM video.
    86	- The user cannot remove it through Settings. Nope-Mode **must** expose
    87	  *Relinquish device owner* → `clearDeviceOwnerApp()`. Without it the only exit
    88	  is a factory reset. Implemented in WS4; do not remove it.
    89	- Only one device owner may exist. Nope-Mode holds that slot for the life of
    90	  the install.
    91	
    92	### 3.2 Provisioning window (historical, now satisfied)
    93	
    94	Device owner can only be set on a device with **zero accounts**:
    95	
    96	```sh
    97	adb shell dpm set-device-owner \
    98	    com.piercingxx.nopemode/.admin.NopeDeviceAdminReceiver
    99	```
   100	
   101	This was provisioned on 2026-08-03 after a factory reset. **It cost one wipe to
   102	learn that opening the Google apps first closes the window.** If device owner is
   103	ever relinquished, regaining it costs another full reset — treat it as
   104	non-renewable.
   105	
   106	---
   107	
   108	## 4. Platform mechanics
   109	
   110	Authoritative behavior of `DevicePolicyManager.setPackagesSuspended`, from
   111	Android documentation. The whole design rests on this, so it is quoted rather
   112	than paraphrased loosely.
   113	
   114	A suspended package:
   115	
   116	- cannot start activities;
   117	- has its **notifications hidden**;
   118	- does **not** appear in the recents / overview screen;
   119	- cannot show toasts, dialogs, or snackbars;
   120	- **cannot play audio or vibrate the device**;
   121	- shows a system "app is paused" dialog when tapped;
   122	- is **grayed out in the launcher**.
   123	
   124	That single call satisfies R2 and R3 completely. No notification listener, no
   125	accessibility service, no DND manipulation is required at this tier.
   126	
   127	### 4.1 Packages that cannot be suspended
   128	
   129	The platform refuses these outright. The picker must exclude them at
   130	**selection time**, not fail at enforcement time:
   131	
   132	- Device admins — **this includes Nope-Mode itself**
   133	- The **active launcher** (suspending it bricks the home screen)
   134	- The required **package installer**, **uninstaller**, and **verifier**
   135	- The **default dialer**
   136	- The **permission controller**
   137	
   138	Two more that the platform *permits* but which must be guarded anyway:
   139	
   140	- **The active input method.** Suspending the keyboard leaves the user unable
   141	  to type — including unable to type their way out. Hard-block it.
   142	- **The default SMS handler.** Permitted, and a legitimate choice for some, but
   143	  it silences 2FA codes. Require an explicit confirmation; never reachable via
   144	  bulk-select.
   145	
   146	`setPackagesSuspended` **returns the array of packages it could not suspend.**
   147	Never discard it (R8).
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## 5. Architecture
   152	
   153	```
   154	        ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
   155	        │           NopeController           │  owns desired state
   156	        │  derive(now, schedules, override)  │  talks to no Android API
   157	        └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘
   158	                           │ desired: Set<packageName>
   159	        ┌──────────────────▼─────────────────┐
   160	        │         Enforcer (interface)       │
   161	        └────────┬──────────────────┬────────┘
   162	                 │                  │
   163	      ┌──────────▼──────┐   ┌───────▼─────────────────┐
   164	      │ SuspendEnforcer │   │    FallbackEnforcer     │
   165	      │  device owner   │   │  listener + a11y        │
   166	      └─────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘
   167	```
   168	
   169	`NopeController` computes *what should be true* and hands it to an `Enforcer`.
   170	It imports nothing from `android.*`. That is what makes the scheduling logic —
   171	the part that must be correct — testable on the JVM with no device.
   172	
   173	Tier selection, re-evaluated whenever admin state changes:
   174	
   175	```
   176	if (dpm.isDeviceOwnerApp(packageName)) SuspendEnforcer else FallbackEnforcer
   177	```
   178	
   179	The active tier must be **visible in the UI at all times**. A user on the
   180	fallback tier is getting weaker protection and has to know it (R8).
   181	
   182	---
   183	
   184	## 6. State model
   185	
   186	The heart of the app. Everything else is plumbing.
   187	
   188	```kotlin
   189	sealed interface Override {
   190	    data object None : Override
   191	    data class ForceOn(val until: Instant?) : Override   // null = indefinite
   192	    data class Break(val until: Instant) : Override      // ALWAYS bounded
   193	}
   194	
   195	fun isActive(now, schedules, override): Boolean = when (override) {
   196	    is Override.ForceOn -> override.until == null || now < override.until
   197	    is Override.Break   -> if (now < override.until) false
   198	                           else scheduleSaysActive(now, schedules)
   199	    Override.None       -> scheduleSaysActive(now, schedules)
   200	}
   201	```
   202	
   203	| Override | Schedule | Result |
   204	|---|---|---|
   205	| `None` | inactive | inactive |
   206	| `None` | active | **active** |
   207	| `ForceOn(null)` | either | **active**, indefinitely |
   208	| `ForceOn(t)`, now < t | either | **active** |
   209	| `ForceOn(t)`, now ≥ t | — | expires → re-derive from schedule |
   210	| `Break(t)`, now < t | active | inactive (break running) |
   211	| `Break(t)`, now ≥ t | active | **active** — break expired, auto-resume |
   212	
   213	**`Break` has no unbounded variant, by construction.** There is no way to
   214	express "off until I say so". This is D7, and it is the difference between a
   215	schedule and a suggestion.
   216	
   217	---
   218	
   219	## 7. Scheduling
   220	
   221	```kotlin
   222	data class Schedule(
   223	    val id: Long,
   224	    val startMinuteOfDay: Int,   // 20:00 -> 1200
   225	    val endMinuteOfDay: Int,     // 08:00 -> 480
   226	    val daysMask: Int,           // bit 0 = Monday .. bit 6 = Sunday
   227	    val enabled: Boolean,
   228	)
   229	```
   230	
   231	**Windows cross midnight.** `end <= start` means the window wraps into the next
   232	day. The shipped default (1200 → 480) does exactly this, so **the wrap is the
   233	common path, not an edge case.** Test it first, before the non-wrapping case.
   234	
   235	`daysMask` refers to the day the window **starts**. A Friday-enabled 20:00→08:00
   236	window runs Friday 20:00 through Saturday 08:00. A user unchecking Saturday
   237	expects Saturday *night* to be unblocked, not Saturday *morning* — say so in the
   238	UI, because both readings are defensible.
   239	
   240	### 7.1 Reconciliation, not event-chasing
   241	
   242	```kotlin
   243	fun shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean
   244	```
   245	
   246	Pure. State is **always** obtained by calling this, never by accumulating alarm
   247	events (D8). Alarms merely prompt re-evaluation. A missed, late, or duplicated
   248	alarm therefore cannot corrupt state — the system is self-healing.
   249	
   250	`reconcile()` runs on: boot completed, alarm fired, app foregrounded, tile
   251	clicked, schedule edited, blocked-list edited, break started or expired,
   252	`TIME_SET`, `TIMEZONE_CHANGED`.
   253	
   254	### 7.2 Alarms
   255	
   256	- `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP, …)` for **the next boundary only**;
   257	  recompute and re-arm after each fire. Never pre-schedule a chain.
   258	- `USE_EXACT_ALARM` (API 33+), plus `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` for the minSdk 24
   259	  range. If `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is false, degrade to
   260	  `setAndAllowWhileIdle` **and show a persistent warning** — an inexact 20:00
   261	  boundary can drift by minutes, which is visible and wrong.
   262	- `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` → re-arm and reconcile. Without this the schedule
   263	  dies at the first reboot, which is exactly the Shizuku failure D1 rejected.
   264	
   265	---
   266	
   267	## 8. Enforcement tiers
   268	
   269	### 8.1 SuspendEnforcer — primary
   270	
   271	```kotlin
   272	dpm.setPackagesSuspended(admin, packages, true)   // engage
   273	dpm.setPackagesSuspended(admin, packages, false)  // release
   274	```
   275	
   276	Order of operations matters for crash safety:
   277	
   278	1. Write intended packages to `suspend_record`.
   279	2. Call `setPackagesSuspended(…, true)`.
   280	3. Inspect the returned failure array; record and surface any failures.
   281	
   282	Releasing reverses it: suspend-false first, then clear `suspend_record` only
   283	for packages that actually released.
   284	
   285	If the process dies between (1) and (2), reconcile-on-boot sees a record with
   286	nothing suspended and re-derives — harmless. If it dies between (2) and (3),
   287	the record is authoritative and the apps get released correctly. **Writing the
   288	record first is what makes a crash recoverable rather than stranding apps.**
   289	
   290	### 8.2 FallbackEnforcer — no device owner
   291	
   292	**a) `NopeNotificationListener : NotificationListenerService`**
   293	On `onNotificationPosted`, if the package is blocked and the mode is active,
   294	`cancelNotification(sbn.key)`; prefer `snoozeNotification(key, duration)` where
   295	it fits, since it suppresses re-post without a visible dismissal.
   296	
   297	> **Stated limitation, which must appear in the UI verbatim in spirit:** the
   298	> notification has already been posted when the listener sees it, so **the alert
   299	> sound may play before suppression**. This tier delivers "the notification goes
   300	> away", not "the notification never made a sound". It does not satisfy R2.
   301	
   302	**b) `NopeAccessibilityService : AccessibilityService`**
   303	On `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED`, read the foreground package; if blocked and
   304	active, launch `BlockedActivity` with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`. Debounce to
   305	avoid launch loops.
   306	
   307	Do **not** use `performGlobalAction(GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK)` as the block — it
   308	fights the user's navigation and behaves inconsistently across launchers.
   309	
   310	---
   311	
   312	## 9. Breaks and anti-bypass
   313	
   314	Adopted from DetoxDroid's "protection always on" and Curbox's graduated
   315	resistance. Without this, a schedule is decoration — at 2am the user simply
   316	turns it off.
   317	
   318	**Baseline (ship in WS7):**
   319	
   320	- **Take a break** offers **5 / 15 / 30 minutes**, matching Focus Mode. No
   321	  custom-duration field, no "until I turn it back on".
   322	- Breaks **auto-resume**. There is no user action required to re-engage.
   323	- A break shows a persistent countdown notification from Nope-Mode itself, so
   324	  it is never ambiguous whether protection is on.
   325	
   326	**Friction (WS7, configurable, default on):**
   327	
   328	- **Minimum interval between breaks** — default 30 minutes. Prevents chaining
   329	  5-minute breaks into an unbounded evening.
   330	- **Break budget** — default 3 per active window. Exhausted means exhausted.
   331	
   332	**Deferred, explicitly out of scope for v1:**
   333	
   334	- Typing a sentence, scanning a QR code, or a commitment password. These are
   335	  proven patterns (Curbox, DetoxDroid) but they are anti-features until the
   336	  basics are solid. Revisit only if the baseline proves too easy to defeat.
   337	
   338	Every friction setting must be **editable only while Nope-Mode is inactive.**
   339	Otherwise the 2am workaround is simply to raise the break budget.
   340	
   341	---
   342	
   343	## 10. Data model (Room)
   344

     3	import android.app.admin.DevicePolicyManager
     4	import android.content.ComponentName
     5	import android.content.Context
     6	import android.util.Log
     7	
     8	/**
     9	 * Which enforcement tier is available, and the one action that gives it up.
    10	 *
    11	 * Nope-Mode has two tiers (design.md §4). [Tier.DEVICE_OWNER] can suspend
    12	 * packages outright; [Tier.FALLBACK] can only cancel notifications after
    13	 * they have already posted, so a sound may escape first. Callers must be able
    14	 * to tell the user which one they are actually on — silently degrading would
    15	 * make the app claim protection it isn't providing.
    16	 */
    17	class DeviceOwnerManager(context: Context) {
    18	
    19	    private val appContext = context.applicationContext
    20	    private val dpm =
    21	        appContext.getSystemService(Context.DEVICE_POLICY_SERVICE) as DevicePolicyManager
    22	
    23	    enum class Tier { DEVICE_OWNER, FALLBACK }
    24	
    25	    val adminComponent: ComponentName
    26	        get() = NopeDeviceAdminReceiver.componentName(appContext)
    27	
    28	    fun isDeviceOwner(): Boolean =
    29	        dpm.isDeviceOwnerApp(appContext.packageName)
    30	
    31	    fun tier(): Tier =
    32	        if (isDeviceOwner()) Tier.DEVICE_OWNER else Tier.FALLBACK
    33	
    34	    /**
    35	     * The exact command to run over ADB to provision. Surfaced in the setup
    36	     * screen because it can only be run on a device with zero accounts — once
    37	     * an account exists the window is closed and reopening it costs a factory
    38	     * reset.
    39	     */
    40	    fun provisioningCommand(): String =
    41	        "adb shell dpm set-device-owner ${appContext.packageName}/" +
    42	            ".admin.NopeDeviceAdminReceiver"
    43	
    44	    /**
    45	     * Give up device owner. Without this the only way off the MDM role is a
    46	     * factory reset, so it is a hard requirement rather than a convenience
    47	     * (design.md §2.2).
    48	     *
    49	     * Callers MUST release every suspended package first — once this returns,
    50	     * [DevicePolicyManager.setPackagesSuspended] is no longer callable and
    51	     * anything still suspended is stranded.
    52	     *
    53	     * @return true if device owner was relinquished.
    54	     */
    55	    fun relinquish(): Boolean {
    56	        if (!isDeviceOwner()) return false
    57	        return try {
    58	            dpm.clearDeviceOwnerApp(appContext.packageName)
    59	            Log.i(TAG, "device owner relinquished")

    61	        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
    62	            Log.e(TAG, "failed to relinquish device owner", e)
    63	            false
    64	        }
    65	    }

    69	    }
